text:
Elena R: quick brain-dump: i've been experimenting with a small "split-decision-agent" that sits on the router and applies a simple A/B hazard policy locally. want feedback on signals + failure modes.
Marco B: curious - why local agent vs central decider?
Elena R: latency and resilience mainly. during cp outages we still want safe fallbacks within 50ms. central still owns policy but agent evaluates short window signals.
Juniper C: ok. what signals are you collecting?
Elena R: p99 latency, accumulated token-timeouts per route, short-circuit 5xx ratio, and a semantic-quality flag we get from async evals. also a small heartbeat from control-plane.
Ravi L: caution: mixing quality signals that come from async evals (minutes delay) with infra signals (seconds) can lead to wrong flips. how do you separate them?
Elena R: we tag signals with "staleness" and only let async-quality cause a bounded soft-degrade (reduce traffic) not immediate hard-fallback. infra signals can trigger hard-fallback.
Marco B: sketch of rule language you showed earlier was nice:
```
rule {
  route: "/api/chat/*"
  hard_triggers: [p99_latency_ms > 400, http_5xx_rate > 0.02]
  soft_triggers: [quality_delta_pct > 5]
  fallback: "model-stable-v2"
  tenant_overrides: {"enterprise": {hard_triggers.p99_latency_ms: 600}}
}
```
Juniper C: ownership question: who hands the agent the fallback list? agent needs to pick compatible targets.
Elena R: control-plane signs a compact policy blob (routes + fallback ids + cohort tags). agent verifies signature and caches the blob. revocations are via a tiny PRL (policy revocation list).
Ravi L: how fast can you revoke? we need secs for high-sev incidents.
Elena R: hybrid approach: push for immediate revokes (fanout via ctrl-notify) + pull PRL every 10s. if push missed, pull enforces state.
Marco B: what about flip-flop? if an agent toggles repeatedly it can thrash KV caches and increase cost.
Juniper C: add hysteresis: require stable condition for T seconds or N requests before a hard flip; plus backoff windows (cooldown).
Elena R: plan: require 3 consecutive windows (30s lookback, sampled every 10s) or a 60s steady-state before permanent flip. also track flip_count and promote auto-escalation to control-plane if flips > 3 in 10m.
Ravi L: metrics to emit: agent.policy_id, agent.mode (passive/emergency/auto), agent.flip_reason, agent.flip_count, agent.reconcile_latency. traces must include policy_id and decision_version.
Juniper C: testing: add chaos tests that drop push notifications and simulate partial policy rollouts; verify PRL and reconciliation logic wins.
Marco B: security: sign with CP KMS key; agent verifies kid/thumbprint. make keys short-lived and rotate weekly. store private key only in CP HSM.
Elena R: runbook sketch:
- passive: agent logs decisions but doesn't route; ops can inspect via dashboard
- emergency: agent can flip on hard_triggers, emits incident event and notifies cp
- auto: agent flips and writes compact event to cp for auditing
RolloutBot: split-agent v0.2 deployed (passive) to router-canary-11 at 1776010025
Ravi L: corner case: tenant-scoped thresholds. ensure agent enforces per-tenant exemptions (e.g., enterprise get higher thresholds). policy blob contains cohort tags for this.
Juniper C: KV-warmup: when switching to fallback, expect cold cache. options: warm synchronously (latency hit) or accept transient increase. Document expectation and include fallback-cost metric.
Elena R: last: add dry-run revoke where agent reports what it would revoke. good for drills.
Marco B: ok action items: elena -> RFC addendum + prototype docs; juniper -> chaos tests + metrics dashboard; ravi -> security key rotation plan.
Elena R: thanks all, i'll draft RFC follow-up and attach prototype links.
OpsBot: note: ensure audit logs include operator id + incident id on any manual revoke.
